definition: casual talk or rumor about the private lives of other people
hook: Gossip started as a compliment, not an insult.
modernAnchor: We swap it at the water cooler and scroll it in comment sections. Gossip never goes out of style.
journey: In Old English, a godsibb was your godparent, a person bound to your family before God.
Godsibb shrank to gossip and widened to any close friend you shared secrets and news with.
By Shakespeare's day, women who gossiped together were assumed to be trading rumor, not just news.
The friend became the talk. Gossip is literally the word for someone who stood as your godparent.
